㊥ (gist) The all-underlined turn is fixed and already reloaded into your Emacs: an operator fragment now shows its intent mark before it instead of a whole-text underline. The drop-in idea holds, with one honest caveat about the mark7 page, and the data shape plus a draft comment for issue 7 are written up in `futon3c/holes/excursions/E-scope-view.md`.

㊬ ("all underlined") The route split your turn into five fragments covering 754 of its 760 characters, and the overlay underlined each operator fragment whole. Tiled fragments underlined whole is the whole turn underlined. The fix in `xiang-scope-overlay.el` gives an operator fragment an empty span and sets its intent's proforma mark before it, the same thing 小象 does on a draft, so your turn reads ㊩ BTW… 🈰 Regarding… ㊭ yes this sounds useful… ㊟ though I'm not sure… 🈖 This would… Ten ERT tests pass, check-parens is clean, and a repaint of the live REPL buffer placed 10 overlays with 5 marks. Commit 30999e93d.

㊣ ("drop-in replacement") Yes, and reading the mark7 page shows why the same module fits. Its painting script is two halves. The first half places every rendered word and formula at an offset in the paper's source, because LaTeXML only stamps blocks and formula columns are approximate. The second half inks three plates, mixes them, writes margin notes and lights passages on hover. The second half is the view. The first half is the same relocation work the Emacs module spends 250 lines on, and the turn-margin page, which renders the record's own text, needs none of it. So the view never relocates. A host that paints over text it does not own supplies anchored segments through an adapter, which mark7 has already computed as its word list.

㊟ ("drop-in") Not everything on the mark7 page moves into the view. The run-level numbers in the banner, the mock-verdict mode, and word placement stay with the page as its adapter. Plates, toggles, ink mixing, hover, margin notes and the glossary rule move.

㊟ ("not sure that Rob had the compiler scopes in mind") I could not read the issue thread from here, since the GitHub query returned nothing, so the note quotes only the title you gave. The draft comment asks Rob directly which "scopes" he meant and what the Augmented Element view needs from a room. Element rooms map cleanly: segments are messages, spans are acts, edges are replies and governing acts, which is your point about Emacs and Matrix.

🈖 (the shape) Segments of text, layers, spans with a kind, a mark, a weight and a note, edges with a relation and label, and a legend that must define every label. Offsets are code points into one segment, the unit the turn records already declare. The 象 adapter has what it needs: the scopes route gives spans and edges, and the turn view route serves the record's text, keyed by record id rather than turn id.

segments.label: writing-coherence/name-what-you-drop
segments.text: Name What You Drop, Not Only What You Inherit. When a section describes what a successor project inherits from a predecessor, listing only the inheritance leaves readers to infer the full extent of the inheritance — which they will do generously.  The remedy is to name, alongside what is taken, what is deliberately dropped.  The drop list is short, explicit, and located in the same eyeshot as the inheritance list; without it, scope is implicit-by-omission and readers will silently over-attribute.  The discipline applies symmetrically: when naming what one is doing with a predecessor's work, name what one is leaving behind.
